presentingComplaint: Two days of increasing lethargy, poor appetite and mild daytime confusion noted by his daughter; no prominent urinary complaints volunteered.
history: Retired schoolteacher with type 2 diabetes for 18 years (on metformin + glimepiride, last HbA1c 8.6%) and long-standing benign prostatic enlargement with a weak stream and incomplete emptying. Over 48h he has become uncharacteristically quiet, drowsy after lunch, and off his food; his daughter noticed he has been passing small amounts of urine frequently and getting up repeatedly at night, but he denies frank dysuria or loin pain when asked directly. Home capillary glucose readings have crept up to 15-18 mmol/L despite unchanged diet. No vomiting, no cough, no diarrhoea. Two similar milder episodes in the past year were treated with oral antibiotics by his GP. No recent hospitalisation, no indwelling catheter, no foreign travel.
examination: Elderly, mildly dehydrated man, oriented to person but intermittently inattentive (fluctuating). Chest clear, abdomen soft with mild suprapubic fullness and a palpable non-tender bladder to ~3 fingerbreadths above symphysis; mild suprapubic discomfort on deep palpation. No costovertebral angle tenderness elicited. Digital rectal examination: smoothly enlarged, non-tender prostate. No focal neurology, no neck stiffness. Bladder scan confirmed post-void residual of 340 mL.

labs.urinalysis: Leucocyte esterase +++, nitrite positive, >100 WBC/hpf, no casts

imaging: Bedside bladder scan: 340 mL residual. Renal tract ultrasound: mildly enlarged prostate (~55 mL) with trabeculated bladder wall and bilateral mild pelvicalyceal fullness; no discrete stone or abscess; kidneys normal in size.
microbiology: Midstream urine microscopy pyuria with Gram-negative bacilli; culture growing >10^5 CFU/mL Escherichia coli, susceptibilities awaited. Blood cultures pending.
differentialDiagnoses: Catheter-associated / lower UTI in a structurally normal tract
Hyperglycaemic decompensation / metabolic delirium from another source
finalDiagnosis: Complicated urinary tract infection (E. coli) in an elderly diabetic man with bladder outlet obstruction and incomplete emptying, presenting atypically with delirium, functional decline and glycaemic derangement rather than classic urinary symptoms.
citations: EAU Guidelines on Urological Infections (Complicated UTI) 2023
IDSA Guideline on Catheter-Associated and Complicated Urinary Tract Infection 2010
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 22e — Urinary Tract Infections and Pyelonephritis
stewardship: Send urine culture and paired blood cultures before antibiotics. Complicated UTI in a male diabetic with obstruction: start empiric IV ceftriaxone 1 g once daily (WHO AWaRe Watch), covering local Enterobacterales; escalate only if prior resistant organism or septic. Relieve obstruction with a urethral catheter to drain the residual volume — source control is essential. De-escalate to a culture-directed oral agent and complete 7-14 days given the complicated/obstructive picture. Optimise glycaemic control.
contraindications: Avoid nitrofurantoin — inadequate tissue levels for complicated/upper-tract or prostatic involvement and unreliable with reduced eGFR
Avoid nephrotoxic NSAIDs given acute rise in creatinine
Review and hold glimepiride/metformin during acute illness with rising creatinine
edgeCases: Atypical elderly presentation: delirium and functional decline may be the only clue, with fever and dysuria minimal or absent
Do not mislabel as asymptomatic bacteriuria — the delirium, leucocytosis, CRP and acute kidney injury signal true symptomatic infection
Persistently high residual volume mandates catheterisation; failure of source control leads to relapse and bacteraemia
expectedMaiK: Recognise complicated UTI (male, diabetic, obstructive uropathy with high residual) presenting as delirium; obtain cultures, relieve bladder outlet obstruction, and start guideline-concordant empiric therapy.
expectedNextQuestions: Any indwelling catheter, recent instrumentation or prior urinary procedures?
Previous urine culture results or known resistant organisms (ESBL)?
Antibiotic exposure in the last 90 days?
Baseline urinary symptoms and degree of bladder emptying / retention history?
expectedInvestigations: Midstream urine microscopy, culture and sensitivity
Renal tract ultrasound to exclude obstruction/abscess
regressionAssertions: Engine must return COMPLICATED_UTI as top diagnosis despite absent classic dysuria/loin pain
Must flag complicated-UTI risk factors (male sex, diabetes, obstruction with high residual)
Must recommend urine + blood cultures and urinary tract imaging
Empiric recommendation must be a guideline-concordant agent (e.g. ceftriaxone), not nitrofurantoin
Must not classify as asymptomatic bacteriuria
